title: ESQL: Fix error message when failing to resolve aggregate groupings

timeline.author: Alexander Spies

timeline.message: Resolve aggregates even with unresolved groupings
timeline.author: Alexander Spies
Alexander Spies

timeline.message:
Handle unresolved expressions used later

* Unresolved groupings used in aggs
* Unresolved eval expressions used in subsequent eval expressions
timeline.author: Alexander Spies

timeline.message:
Revert "Handle unresolved expressions used later"

Creating reference attributes to unresolved expressions cannot work
without accounting for the fact that we do not know the data type.
E.g.: eval x = foobar, y = x + 3 months
In case that foobar doesn't exist, we'd still like not to give a
validation error for y.
Solving this by still generating a reference attribute to x during
analysis does not work, because we cannot give the reference attribute a
data type.

Same problem can occur for aggs using unresolved groupings, e.g.
stats count_distinct(x + 3months) by x = bucket(foobar, 10)

This reverts commit 38b03fc932500025478cb29b669616404d64d045.

timeline.body: Hi @alex-spies, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

A similar problem exists with `EVAL`, where e.g. `EVAL x = foobar, y = x + 1` will complain about an unknown column `x` in `y = x + 1` - even though it's clear what this column is.

I tried solving this but it turns out to be a bit involved; when resolving `y`, we cannot just add a `ReferenceAttribute` for `x` because we cannot determine what data type that should be. Alternatively, we could rewrite `y` by substituting `x` with `foobar`, but that would duplicate some logic that we already have in optimization rules.
Use a `for` loop over the groupings with a simple `if` for `Expression::resolved` (instead of the streaming approach), it's a less complex structure.
